notes: A Lothian bus day ticket costs 5.50 GBP (via the app) and the airport tram 7 GBP. Take the train to Stirling and Loch Lomond, and the 37 bus to Rosslyn. The city is hilly but walkable.

August brings the Fringe and Tattoo festivals (3,000 shows). Hotels cost three times as much, so book months ahead. Summer is 15-20°C with changeable weather, and daylight lasts until 22:00. June and July are ideal.
The castle costs 20 GBP and online tickets are mandatory. The museums (National, Galleries) are free. A pub lunch costs 15-20 GBP, a whisky tasting 25 GBP, and a tip is 10%.
Try haggis, Cullen skink, Scotch pie, cranachan and Irn-Bru. For whisky, Islay is smoky and Speyside is sweet.
You can get four seasons in an hour: carry a raincoat and dress in layers. The wind is fierce on Calton Hill and Arthur's Seat.
Harry Potter spots: Victoria Street, Greyfriars, the Elephant House, and room 552 at the Balmoral Hotel.

stops.name: Edinburgh Castle
stops.tips: A fortress on a volcanic rock: the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny and the 13:00 one o'clock gun. Book timed tickets online, as they sell out.

stops.name: Royal Mile Walk
stops.tips: 1.6 km from the castle to Holyrood. Take in St Giles' Cathedral (Thistle Chapel) and the closes (narrow alleys), and join a Mary King's Close tour.

stops.name: Deacon Brodie's Tavern
stops.tips: Named after the thieving councillor who inspired Dr Jekyll. Try haggis, neeps and tatties.

stops.name: The Real Mary King's Close
stops.tips: Buried 17th-century streets beneath the road, with tales of the plague. Book ahead.

stops.name: Scotch Whisky Experience
stops.tips: A barrel ride and a tasting, plus a collection of 3,000 bottles. On Castlehill.

backups.name: Oink Victoria Street
backups.tips: Hog roast sandwiches. Expect a queue.

backups.name: Camera Obscura
backups.tips: An illusion tower from 1835. A swap for Mary King's Close if you have children.

stops.name: Arthur's Seat
stops.tips: An extinct volcano, 251 m high. 45 minutes from Holyrood Park, with panoramic views of the city and the Firth of Forth. Expect wind.

stops.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
stops.tips: The monarch's palace in Scotland. See Mary, Queen of Scots' rooms and the ruined abbey.

stops.name: The Sheep Heid Inn
stops.tips: Scotland's oldest pub, dating from 1360 (a queen once visited). It has a skittles alley and a village setting in Duddingston.

stops.name: Calton Hill
stops.tips: The National Monument (an unfinished Parthenon) and the Nelson Monument. The best postcard view of the city, especially at sunset.

stops.name: Dean Village
stops.tips: A medieval milling village on the Water of Leith. A fairy tale within the city.

backups.name: Dynamic Earth
backups.tips: A science centre telling the history of the planet. A swap for Holyrood if you have children.

backups.name: Holyrood 9A
backups.tips: Burgers and craft beer, just off the Royal Mile.

stops.name: National Gallery of Scotland
stops.tips: Free, on the Mound. See Titian, Raeburn's The Skating Minister and The Monarch of the Glen.

stops.name: Princes Street Gardens & Scott Monument
stops.tips: A Gothic rocket of a monument with 287 steps. The gardens look up to the castle and have a floral clock.

stops.name: Stockbridge Market & Circus Lane
stops.tips: The market runs on Sundays. Circus Lane is a flower-lined back street, popular for photos.

stops.name: The Scran & Scallie
stops.tips: Tom Kitchin's gastropub, serving Scottish produce.

stops.name: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
stops.tips: A botanic garden founded in 1670. The glasshouses are ticketed, and Inverleith Hill has views of the castle.

backups.name: Scottish National Portrait Gallery
backups.tips: A neo-Gothic red building. Free, with portraits of Mary Stuart.

backups.name: The Pantry
backups.tips: Brunch in Stockbridge. Expect a queue.

stops.name: Rosslyn Chapel
stops.tips: The 1446 chapel from The Da Vinci Code. See the Apprentice Pillar and hundreds of carvings. Take the 37 bus, 40 minutes.

stops.name: Roslin Glen Walk
stops.tips: A stream valley below the chapel, with castle ruins.

stops.name: The Original Rosslyn Inn
stops.tips: A village inn. Pub lunch.

stops.name: Flotterstone, Pentland Hills
stops.tips: Hills south of the city. Walk to Glencorse Reservoir past grazing sheep. Take the 101 bus.

backups.name: Craigmillar Castle
backups.tips: A ruined castle where Mary Stuart took refuge. Inside the city, so a swap for the Pentlands.

backups.name: Flotterstone Inn
backups.tips: A pub at the entrance to the Pentlands.

stops.name: Stirling Castle
stops.tips: 50 minutes by train. The castle of the Scottish kings, with the Great Hall and views of the Wallace Monument.

stops.name: National Wallace Monument
stops.tips: A 67 m tower to the Braveheart hero, marking the Battle of Stirling Bridge (1297). 246 steps.

stops.name: Stirling Old Town Lunch
stops.tips: A café beside the Old Town Jail. Try the Cullen skink soup.

stops.name: Balloch, Loch Lomond
stops.tips: 1 hour by tour or train. Scotland's largest loch, with Balloch Castle park and boat trips (summer).

stops.name: Luss
stops.tips: A stone village on the loch shore. Watch the sunset from the pier (by tour or car).

backups.name: Doune Castle
backups.tips: The castle of Monty Python and Outlander. A swap for the Wallace Monument (by car).

backups.name: The Portcullis
backups.tips: A pub at the castle gate in Stirling.

stops.name: Royal Yacht Britannia
stops.tips: The Queen's yacht from 1953 to 1997. At Leith's Ocean Terminal, with an audio guide.

stops.name: The Shore, Leith
stops.tips: The old harbour. This is the Trainspotting district, with Michelin-starred restaurants.

stops.name: Fishers Leith
stops.tips: Seafood in the harbour tower. Open since 1991.

stops.name: Water of Leith Walkway
stops.tips: A 5 km riverside path from Leith to Dean Village, passing Antony Gormley statues in the water.

stops.name: Surgeons' Hall Museums
stops.tips: A surgical museum covering the body snatchers Burke and Hare. Only if you have a strong stomach.

backups.name: The Kitchin
backups.tips: Michelin-starred. Lunch menu, so book ahead.

backups.name: Portobello Beach
backups.tips: A city beach with a Victorian promenade. A swap for Leith.

stops.name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
stops.tips: The statue of Greyfriars Bobby the dog. Harry Potter names appear on the gravestones (Tom Riddle).

stops.name: The Elephant House Breakfast
stops.tips: The café where Rowling wrote (now reopened). The back room has views of the castle.

stops.name: National Museum of Scotland
stops.tips: Dolly the sheep and the Lewis chessmen. Free, with a roof terrace.

stops.name: Waverley Tram to the Airport
stops.tips: 35 minutes to the airport by tram. Farewell.

backups.name: Mums Great Comfort Food
backups.tips: On Forrest Road. Sausages and mash.

backups.name: Grassmarket Saturday Market
backups.tips: A farmers' and crafts market on Saturdays.
